newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end near day's lows, eyes on ABB.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end near day's lows, eyes on ABB.

text.p: After initial advances to an all-time high, Swiss shares ended a volatile day back down near the day's lows on Thursday.
Dealers said the session was marked by selective buying and special situations.
Wednesday's Wall Street weakness was initially shrugged off but early losses in New York led to profit taking. U.S. stock developments would continue to influence the Swiss market, one dealer said.
The market focused on ABB, which slumped on 1996 group net profits that were below expectations, traders said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell 19.1 points, or 0.42 percent, to 4,519.9 after touching a all-time high at 4,570.5.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 6.87 points to 2,869.81.
ABB ended down 96 francs, or 5.3 percent, at 1,714.
SMH continued its recent slump, giving up 23 francs to 843. The company recently reported preliminary 1996 results, saying that group net rose to 282 million Swiss francs from 273 million.
Among chemicals and pharmaceuticals, trade was active in share rights for Ciba Specialty Chemicals, which gave up 2.85 francs to 95.20. Novartis and Roche were also lower.
Banks and insurers performed better than the market, reportedly profiting from a positive interest rate outlook.
SBC jumped 4.50 francs to 279.50. CS Group and insurers Winterthur and Baloise also posted solid gains. UBS bearers edged slighty up, advancing one franc to 1,308.
